evidence.claim: Bangladesh voted in favour of the UN General Assembly resolution demanding aid access and civilian protection in Ukraine.
evidence.title: Bangladesh votes in favour of Ukraine on UN resolution
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh voted in favour of the UN General Assembly resolution demanding aid access and civilian protection in Ukraine.
evidence.source_locator: Article text on the March 24 UNGA vote
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Local reporting quoting the UN vote outcome and Bangladesh's position; indirect but specific.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to the Ukraine crisis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State foreign-policy choice under Hasina's government.
contrary_evidence: The vote supports peace and civilian protection, but it does not show broader conflict-management consistency by itself.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh abstained from the UN General Assembly resolution calling for Russia to be held accountable for violating international law by invading Ukraine.
evidence.title: Bangladesh abstains from UN vote against Russia
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh abstained from the UN General Assembly resolution calling for Russia to be held accountable for violating international law by invading Ukraine.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed local reporting on the specific vote and Bangladesh's position.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State foreign-policy choice under Hasina's government.
contrary_evidence: This is a contrary data point against a uniformly hard line on Russia.
The article notes Bangladesh had voted differently on earlier Ukraine resolutions.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh said the UN Charter's role in maintaining international peace and security depends on states refraining from force and respecting sovereignty, territorial integrity, and peaceful settlement of disputes.
evidence.title: 2022 Statement DPR Special Committee on the Charter of the UN
evidence.publisher: Permanent Mission of Bangladesh to the United Nations, New York
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh said the UN Charter's role in maintaining international peace and security depends on states refraining from force and respecting sovereignty, territorial integrity, and peaceful settlement of disputes.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary 2022 government statement at the UN.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and relevant to lawful security norms.
contrary_evidence: Normative language does not establish implementation in specific crises.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh warned that rapid technological advances, including artificial intelligence and biotechnology, could pose risks to international peace and security and require vigilance against malicious use.
evidence.title: 2022 Statement Counsellor Thematic Debate: Other Disarmament Measures And International Security
evidence.publisher: Permanent Mission of Bangladesh to the United Nations, New York
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh warned that rapid technological advances, including artificial intelligence and biotechnology, could pose risks to international peace and security and require vigilance against malicious use.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and directly relevant to dual-use/catastrophic-risk governance.
contrary_evidence: This is broad multilateral language, not a Bangladesh-specific policy implementation record.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh stated that outer space should be used exclusively for peaceful purposes and described access to space as a global common good.
evidence.title: 2022 Statement Counsellor Thematic Debate: Outer Space (disarmament aspects)
evidence.publisher: Permanent Mission of Bangladesh to the United Nations, New York
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh stated that outer space should be used exclusively for peaceful purposes and described access to space as a global common good.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and relevant to lawful, peaceful security framing.
contrary_evidence: The statement is aspirational and does not show concrete national capability management.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh said it was working with the ICC prosecution team and the OIC to ensure justice for Rohingya women and youth and framed a safe, dignified future for Rohingya as requiring a lasting solution beyond camp containment.
evidence.title: 2022 Statement HEPR Rohingya Crisis
evidence.publisher: Permanent Mission of Bangladesh to the United Nations, New York
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh said it was working with the ICC prosecution team and the OIC to ensure justice for Rohingya women and youth and framed a safe, dignified future for Rohingya as requiring a lasting solution beyond camp containment.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary 2022 government statement at the UN.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and relevant to peacebuilding and accountability.
contrary_evidence: The statement is humanitarian and justice-oriented, not a concrete bilateral settlement result.

evidence.claim: UN peacekeeping described Bangladesh as one of the largest contributors to UN peacekeeping and noted that Bangladesh joined the UNPOL component of UNFICYP in November 2022, with an explicit commitment to increasing female peacekeepers.
evidence.title: UNFICYP welcomes Bangladesh and Indonesia at UNPOL flag-raising ceremony
evidence.excerpt: UN peacekeeping described Bangladesh as one of the largest contributors to UN peacekeeping and noted that Bangladesh joined the UNPOL component of UNFICYP in November 2022, with an explicit commitment to increasing female peacekeepers.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UN peacekeeping mission page with dated 2022 deployment details.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and relevant to peaceful international security roles.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional, not personal; still relevant to Hasina-era state conduct.
contrary_evidence: This shows peacekeeping participation, not a direct ruler-level peace decision in a crisis.

evidence.claim: Bangladeshi peacekeepers deployed since 14 January 2022 helped protect civilians and UN personnel in and around Bamako.
evidence.title: UN Police honour peacekeepers in Bamako and Goundam
evidence.excerpt: Bangladeshi peacekeepers deployed since 14 January 2022 helped protect civilians and UN personnel in and around Bamako.
evidence.source_locator: Article body describing the Bangladeshi Formed Police Unit
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UN peacekeeping mission report on a 2022 deployment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State institutional conduct under Hasina's government, not a personal field command action.
contrary_evidence: This is peace-support activity, not proof of broader foreign-policy restraint.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh was trying to stop Rohingya refugees from risking their lives in boats to Southeast Asia amid fears that 2022 could be one of the deadliest years at sea for the group.
evidence.title: Bangladesh tries to stop Rohingya risking their lives at sea - official
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh was trying to stop Rohingya refugees from risking their lives in boats to Southeast Asia amid fears that 2022 could be one of the deadliest years at sea for the group.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting carried by Euronews; strong but still secondary.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and relevant to regional stability and refugee management.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government policy environment under Hasina's administration.
contrary_evidence: This addresses humanitarian management and deterrence, not a negotiated peace settlement.
